Germany had already committed in its National Security Strategy to average at least 2% of GDP for defense.","notes":["The excerpt says the summit would adopt the plans; it does not specifically state that Germany participated in drafting or adopting them."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0022-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Witnesses before the Hamburg parliamentary investigation committee said Scholz gave differing accounts of his contacts with Warburg Bank co-owner Christian Olearius: initially citing tax secrecy, later saying he had only listened passively, and subsequently invoking memory gaps.
